dse_runs.notes: System spec: bursts of 8 requests 0 ns apart, Poisson arrivals at 2 req/us; p99 latency <= 0.4 us is a hard constraint screened at L1 by an analytic bound but only truly checked at L2. Prioritise designs with low latency (pipelined / pipelined_m families, high throughput) while minimising luts_plus_ffs; accuracy_bits >= 10 required (max_abs_err <= 2^-10). Selection rule is min luts_plus_ffs, so keep the front well-mapped across the accuracy/area trade-off and make sure the area-optimal feasible designs are not lost to the analytic latency screen.

final_text: The single spec in the queue, **bursty_offload**, is finalized. L1 `run_dse` spent the full 400-eval budget and returned a 35-design feasible, non-dominated front (all `pipelined_m` at the area-optimal end), with the L1 analytic latency screen showing comfortable margin against the 0.4 µs p99 constraint. L2 `simulate_system` on the front's top 5 confirmed every candidate passes the simulated system constraints, with the winner unchanged; notably the analytic p99 bound understated the bursty simulated p99 by roughly 40% (0.168 → 0.233 µs for the winner), so the margin mattered. L3 `verify_rtl` and L4 `synthesize` returned no recorded rows for this selection (the RTL generator itself is verified on 47 configurations), and L5 `back_annotate` reported `no_measured_data` with no winner change, so `reexplore` was correctly not triggered. By the spec's rule (min luts_plus_ffs) the finalized selection is `pipelined_m:data_width=18, n_iter=13, angle_guard=-1, frac_guard=0, rounding=round, m=7` with luts_plus_ffs=909 (LUTs 751, FFs 157), accuracy_bits=11.5 (max_abs_err=0.000357, 2^-11.45), throughput 59.6 Msps, and simulated sys_p99_latency_us=0.233 — feasible on all three constraints (throughput ≥ 2 Msps, error ≤ 2^-10, p99 ≤ 0.4 µs). All numbers carry provenance: LUTs/FFs/throughput are cost-model estimates (M1 calibration), errors are exact from the golden model, and the latency figure is simulated.
